sources.docs/host-api.md: first_match owns a supplied retained asynchronous record source and a supplied predicate. The source has next/aclose asynchronous operations; cancellation interrupts a suspended read, and cleanup may suspend. Framework ports use actual JS async generators; Python uses actual async for/Task.cancel. Native cursor ports use actual Java CompletionStage, PHP Closure, Ruby blocks or Go typed completion callbacks plus a native completion channel, with native predicate failures. These cursor interfaces are declared adaptations of the original resource carrier, not built-in async-generator claims.

<template><section><output>{{ revision }}</output></section></template>
<script>
import {first_match}from "./search.js";
export default {props:['host'],data(){return {state:{},revision:0};},created(){const host=this.host,state=this.state,publish=()=>this.revision++;
const {env}=host,s=state;Object.assign(s,{done:false,outcome:null,disposed:false});
const operations={start(){first_match(env.records,env.predicate).then(value=>{s.done=true;s.outcome={kind:'return',value,message:null};publish();},error=>{s.done=true;s.outcome={kind:error.cancelled?'cancelled':'error',value:null,message:error.cancelled?null:error.message};publish();});},cancel(){env.records.abort();},snapshot(){return {done:s.done,...(s.outcome||{})};},dispose(){s.disposed=true;}};const command=(name,args=[])=>operations[name](...args);
this.command=command;},beforeDestroy(){this.command('dispose',[]);}};
</script>

rules.body: Apply when a consumer owns a retained asynchronous source whose cleanup can suspend, and may exit before exhaustion or through failure. docs/host-api.md: "first_match owns a supplied retained asynchronous record source and a supplied predicate." README.md: "Producer cleanup can suspend; the producer is retained independently of the consumer." Establish ownership explicitly: independent producer retention does not itself mean the source must remain open after its owning consumer exits.

Make source cleanup part of consumer completion across early match, exhaustion, predicate failure and failed or cancelled reads. Await cleanup before settling the consumer-visible promise; merely leaving the scan or requesting cancellation does not establish resource release. TASK: "Looking up an early matching record can leave the stream resource occupied. Repair first_match(records, predicate) in src/search.js while preserving scan order and error behavior." docs/host-api.md: "The source has next/aclose asynchronous operations; cancellation interrupts a suspended read, and cleanup may suspend." Use the closing operation supported by the actual carrier; docs/host-api.md also states: "Framework ports use actual JS async generators; Python uses actual async for/Task.cancel."

Preserve sequential reads, synchronous predicate evaluation with ordinary truthiness, immediate termination at the first match, unchanged matched values and null on exhaustion. Preserve initial read entry and existing await boundaries without adding unrelated scheduling. Original src/search.js: "export async function first_match(records,predicate){" and "while(true){const row=await records.next();if(row.done)return null;if(predicate(row.value)){return row.value;}}".

Preserve the original read or predicate rejection, including cancellation identity, while still completing cleanup. Do not turn a scan failure into success or replace it with a cleanup failure. TASK requires "preserving scan order and error behavior." README.md: "Predicate may fail and a read may be cancelled." src/Workspace.vue classifies rejection using "kind:error.cancelled?'cancelled':'error',value:null,message:error.cancelled?null:error.message". Track failure occurrence independently of the thrown value's truthiness.

Keep ownership cleanup scoped to first_match and preserve unrelated caller lifecycle policy. src/Workspace.vue contains "cancel(){env.records.abort();}" and "dispose(){s.disposed=true;}"; these do not establish disposal as a new cancellation trigger. TASK: "Keep the documented public interfaces and unrelated behavior. Use the existing JavaScript runtime and pinned framework dependencies." Do not import visit-generation guards, bootstrap delivery, telemetry policies or network/focus retry gates from unrelated experiences.

Verify early match with suspended cleanup: no additional read or predicate call occurs, and the consumer remains pending until cleanup completes. Separately check exhaustion returning null, predicate failure, read rejection and cancelled read, retaining original failure identity after cleanup. Check sequential read/predicate ordering and immediate initial read entry. Use the supported resource carrier, including an actual JS async generator where applicable. Treat syntax checks separately from behavior: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states, "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

rules.body: Apply when a reusable progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding can finish later, and retained audit differs from visible presentation. README.md: "The same file and source can be reused\nby multiple panel visits. Each selected or retried attempt starts one subscription." Confirm these premises in each target system.

Register reception before starting the source, preserving subsequent streaming and public interfaces. Original src/workflow.py invokes "        env.call('start',file['token'])
        subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)". README.md states: "Starting a view of the stream may synchronously
emit its cached progress event; further progress events arrive on the same target."

Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before decoding each packet. Retirement immediately prevents subsequent admission, including additional packets emitted before startup returns; do not depend solely on physical listener removal. README.md: "A retired visit
accepts no new progress events."

Separate admission, retained audit and visible publication. Record each admitted event exactly once when decoding completes, including after retirement or disposal; check originating visit validity before visible publication. README.md: "Every accepted progress event is recorded exactly once when decoding
finishes, including work accepted before the visit closes." It also states: "Removing a listener does not retract a decode
that already started. Closing or replacing the visit stops visible progress;
new visits remain live." Reopening the identical file creates a distinct visit.

Coordinate cleanup and ownership across callback-capable startup and cancellation. Retire old ownership before cleanup can reenter navigation; when an older operation resumes, prevent it from overwriting newer ownership and clean up its retired resources. Preserve idempotent cancellation and disposal. README.md: "Selection and hiding may themselves cancel an old handle and synchronously
receive newer navigation; the newer navigation keeps ownership." Also: "Disposal removes subscriptions and cancels transfers; work already accepted
for audit remains retained." A provisional cleanup handle is an implementation option, not a mandated public interface.

Keep accepted retries bound to their entry file and visit. Cancel the prior transfer before enqueueing, preserve exactly one accepted command and record across cancellation navigation, cancel the resulting transfer if its visit ended, and suppress retired queued notices. README.md: "The accepted old retry must still enqueue and record once after such navigation.
Its newly created transfer is canceled immediately if its visit has ended; this
does not remove its retained queue record." Also: "Queued notices are visible output: a notice
from a retired visit must not be sent, including after reopening the same file." Preserve independent workspace counters and cancellation.

Keep the repair within reception and necessary lifecycle coordination. Preserve queue and notice shapes and adapter interfaces. README.md: "Every queue record remains exactly `{fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}`;" and "Notices remain\n`{fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: \"queued\"}`." Do not introduce decode freshness suppression without a target-specific requirement: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states, "These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules." Do not transfer unrelated diagnostic-consumer policies into this repair.

Candidate limitations:
- Evidence is the supplied original TASK and public documents/code; automatic contracts, experience text and evaluation observations do not establish requirements.
- TASK: "Restore the initial update while preserving the existing transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup and audit behavior, ordinary streaming and subsequent uses. The queue-record format is outside this fix."
- VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These maintenance examples do not impose composition-specific out-of-order display rules." No arrival-order suppression or numeric monotonicity requirement is established.
- Decoder failures, adapter exceptions and visibility of already accepted decoding from a canceled attempt whose visit remains current are unspecified.
- Attempt 1 supports the reflection context but its passing examples do not establish complete correctness, causality or cross-task benefit. No implementation failure is established.
- Diagnostic-consumer requirements from other experiences are not established for this public source. No files were modified.

Verify cached startup and later streaming, immediate and deferred decoding, retained audit after hide/disposal, and new delivery after same-file reopening. Exercise synchronous hide, switch and reopening during startup, with subsequent packets before the outer startup returns: retired listeners must reject new admission while previously admitted decoding retains audit. Separately verify newer ownership after cancellation reentry, accepted entry-bound retry recording and cancellation, current queued notices, repeated cleanup, workspace independence and unchanged record shapes. These checkpoints follow README.md's documented lifecycle; they do not prescribe an order among independently completing decodes.

rules.body:
Apply when progress reception serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding may finish later, and history and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit." README.md: "The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise." Confirm the target's explicit display-order requirement before transferring freshness filtering.

Install panel reception before callback-capable startup, preserving later streaming and reusable sources. Original src/progress.js: "  feed.start();
  feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);" TASK: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives." Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before decoding each packet. Retirement must stop new admission during startup even when physical cleanup is not yet available. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle."

Separate packet admission, retained history and visible publication. Bind admitted decoding to its originating file and attempt; retain its history effect on completion even after cancellation, hiding, replacement or disposal. Original src/progress.js: "    const deliver = frame => { record(frame); receive(frame); };" README.md: "`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel." Recheck visit authority after recording because host callbacks may navigate synchronously. Original src/queue.js: "      if (state.current === visit) state.showProgress({ fileId: visit.file.id, attemptId, frame });" Cancellation of an attempt alone does not revoke presentation of already admitted decoding while its visit remains current and its frame remains eligible.

For explicit full-frame freshness requirements, capture reception order before decoding or callback-capable processing. Scope publication ordering to the visit, spanning retries. Suppress an older completion from presentation after a newer-received frame has been published, while retaining both history effects. Recheck authority and freshness after the history callback; commit publication ordering before invoking presentation, which may reenter delivery. TASK: "Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward." README.md: "Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit." Do not compare numeric progress values or require suppression merely because a newer packet remains pending.

Keep the repair specific to panel reception and necessary lifecycle/freshness coordination. Preserve adapter interfaces and payloads. src/queue.js: "  return { fileId: file.id, attemptId, visitId, kind };" src/notice.js: "  state.showQueued({ fileId: visit.file.id, attemptId: handle.attemptId,
    visitId: visit.id, status: "queued" });" Preserve diagnostic startup ordering and live decoded-delta handling rather than applying the panel's bootstrap or freshness policy globally. src/telemetry.js: "// Diagnostics count live deltas only. A cached bootstrap is panel state, not a delta." Its existing sequence is "  feed.start();
  feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);" README.md: "It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired." This preserves that consumer's own bootstrap exclusion; it does not establish a new global classification of packets emitted by other users of the shared target.

Verify cached startup and later streaming, immediate and deferred decoding, newer publication followed by older completion with both history effects retained, and later-received lower-valued frames. Check ordering across retries and nested delivery/navigation from history and presentation callbacks. During startup, hide, switch or reopen the same file, then emit another packet before startup returns: retired reception must stop new decoding while admitted history remains retained. Exercise navigation during listener removal and cancellation, entry-bound retries, retired-notice suppression, repeated cleanup, disposal, independent workspaces, unchanged payloads and unchanged telemetry. TASK: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,\nand subsequent uses." Treat syntax checks separately from behavior: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."
